subject: Private offer packaging: node-hour + usage add-on and channel pass-through routing
messages:
From: Mark Jensen <mark.jensen@freshhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FreshHealth private offer — packaging questions

Marissa, Irene —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and finance asked me to clarify how Redwood is planning to package the private offer for FreshHealth. A few specific questions so we can map to our internal chargeback model: 

1) Do you plan to sell a single SKU that represents a reserved node-hour commitment (e.g., node-hour/month) plus a separate "usage add-on" SKU billed per 100k tokens, or will this be a bundled SKU with blended pricing?
2) How will reseller/distributor margins be represented on the invoice? We need a clean pass-through so our downstream ISV partner can reconcile.
3) Any onboarding or one-time credits we can expect to offset the first-month delta?

If you can share a sample term sheet and the channel margin waterfall (how much goes to distributor vs reseller vs Redwood), that will help speed procurement.

Cheers,
Mark Jensen
VP Procurement
FreshHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FreshHealth private offer — packaging questions

Mark —

Thanks — great questions. High level proposal below; attached I'll send a concise term sheet and a separate workbook for the channel margin waterfall. Please let me know which line items you want visible on the invoice (we can show distributor/reseller splits or roll them into a single net price).

Proposal (recommended):
- Primary SKU: "Reserved Node-Hours" — monthly commitment priced per node-hour (covers reserved capacity, baseline SLA).
- Secondary SKU: "Usage Add-on (per 100k tokens)" — metered SKU for burst/overage beyond reserved throughput; billed monthly.
- Optional: "Burst Credit Pack" prepaid token packs for predictable high-volume months (discount vs ad hoc usage).
- One-time onboarding credit: Redwood offers a $25k credit applied to month 1 invoice to offset migration/testing costs (subject to deal threshold).

Channel pass-through / margin suggestion:
- Distributor uplift: 5% of list (visible line item or netted).
- Reseller commission: 10% of list (commonly netted to reseller).
- Redwood net = list - distributor - reseller.

Notes/ops:
- We can create an invoice mapping that exposes three lines (List price, Distributor fee, Reseller fee) so FreshHealth sees the split. If you prefer a net-only invoice, we can deliver that as well; the accounting downstream is identical if both sides agree on the waterfall.
- For private offers on AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace, the distributor routing varies by marketplace (AWS supports explicit pass-through lines; GCP often nets). Ben, can you confirm recommended invoice path for AWS private offers and if any Marketplace tax handling is needed?

I'll attach the term sheet and channel workbook after I run them by legal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FreshHealth private offer — packaging questions

Marissa / Mark —

Confirming operational details from the marketplace side:
- AWS Private Offer: we can expose the distributor and reseller fee lines in the invoice metadata when the partner is set up as a reseller in the private offer. That shows up in the chargeback UI and we can export it for reconciliation.
- GCP Marketplace: tends to be netted; to show splits we'd need a separate reconciliation report (we can push one monthly).
- Azure Marketplace: supports pass-through but requires correct invoice routing (partner id + reseller mapping).

Tax & billing note: Marketplace platforms sometimes calculate VAT/GST differently for the "list" vs the "net" price. If FreshHealth needs explicit VAT handling, we should align territories now.

Operational ask: please confirm whether FreshHealth prefers (A) invoice that shows all three lines (List / Distributor / Reseller) or (B) a single net line with a monthly reconciliation report. Option A is cleaner for your procurement team; Option B is less noisy on the customer invoice but requires the reconciliation feed.

Ben
Director, Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference

1) I'll circulate a redlined term sheet (attached) that includes the $25k onboarding credit and the waterfall expressed as both visible invoice lines and an alternative netted invoice format. Please indicate which you prefer.
2) I'll attach the channel margin workbook (Channel_Margin_Workbook.xlsx) showing sample math for your FY26 forecast (distributor 5%, reseller 10%, Redwood net).
